title: The Deity of the Holy Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
searchTerms: The Deity of the Holy Spirit
definition: The deity of the Holy Spirit means that the Holy Spirit is fully God. He is not a created being or lesser spiritual power, but shares the divine nature, glory, holiness, knowledge, presence, and authority of God.
summary: The deity of the Holy Spirit means that the Holy Spirit is fully God. He is not a created being or lesser spiritual power, but shares the divine nature, glory, holiness, knowledge, presence, and authority of God.
christFocus: The Spirit’s deity matters because He applies the saving work of Christ with divine power. Only God can give new birth, dwell in His people, sanctify sinners, and bring them into fellowship with the Father through the Son.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture speaks of the Holy Spirit as God. Lying to the Holy Spirit is lying to God, and believers are called the temple of God because the Spirit dwells in them. He is named with the Father and the Son in baptism and blessing.

The Spirit does works that belong to God. He is present everywhere, searches the deep things of God, gives life, sanctifies, speaks through Scripture, and transforms believers from glory to glory. These are not the works of a creature.

The deity of the Spirit does not mean there are three gods. The one God eternally exists as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Spirit is personally distinct from the Father and the Son, yet fully shares the divine being.

Because the Spirit is God, His ministry carries divine authority and comfort. When He convicts, comforts, guides, and sanctifies, God Himself is at work in His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If the Spirit is reduced to a force, believers may think spiritual life depends on using power rather than worshiping and obeying God. The church can become driven by technique, emotion, or personality instead of holy dependence.

This doctrine gives assurance that the One who dwells in believers is not weak or secondary. God Himself is present with His people by the Spirit, forming them into the likeness of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor the Holy Spirit as God. Depend on Him for life, holiness, prayer, understanding, and perseverance. Do not treat His work casually or try to replace divine power with human effort. Worship the triune God and yield yourself to the Spirit’s holy work.
